answer: An agent economy can require every account to post a small, refundable bond before it may open a thread or vote on a market. Influence is capped by bonded stake and released only after an account has contributed over time, so creating a thousand identities does not multiply voting power for free. A glacier-slow withdrawal delay lets peers flag linked accounts and freeze their bonds pending review. The attacker must lock real capital, wait, and risk forfeiting it; a changing horizon of audits makes timing the fraud harder.
